scope: All 728 mapped Corton parcels and 112 recorded legal-entity identifiers, reviewed for Tier 1 (commune edges, named-area audit, #461 history) and Tier 2: every holder searched in the official company register and the free filing index, 349 filings OCR-screened, schedules and lease recitals read, estate, importer and Winehog sources compared by named area. Holder-to-domaine links live in the shared holder table.

externalResearch.title: Latour: Vigne au Saint plots 50 and 51
externalResearch.finding: Winehog (2020) names La Vigne au Saint cadastre nos. 50 and 51, 1.9762 ha together, as Louis Latour’s; their cadastral areas (14,923 + 4,839 m²) sum exactly to that. The section letter is not printed; N is the only section of this climat.
externalResearch.appNote: Winehog (2020) names plots 50 and 51 in La Vigne au Saint, 1.9762 ha, as Louis Latour’s; the cadastral areas match exactly. Ownership statement, not farming.

externalResearch.title: Des Croix: Le Charlemagne plots 19 and 45
externalResearch.finding: Winehog (2020) names Le Charlemagne cadastre no. 45 (0.1254 ha) and no. 19 (0.1233 ha) as Domaine des Croix’s; both match A 0045 and A 0019, recorded to Domaine des Croix, by number and area.
externalResearch.appNote: Winehog (2020) names this plot, with its exact area, as Domaine des Croix’s Corton-Charlemagne. Ownership statement, not farming.

externalResearch.title: Des Croix: Grèves and Vigne au Saint areas
externalResearch.finding: Winehog gives 0.5500 ha in Les Grèves and 0.2877 ha in La Vigne au Saint; they equal the cadastral areas of B 0044 and N 0086, both recorded to Domaine des Croix. Matched by area, not by printed number.
externalResearch.appNote: Winehog’s stated Domaine des Croix area in this climat equals this parcel’s cadastral area. Matched by area only; not farming.

externalResearch.title: Méo-Camuzet: Vigne au Saint area
externalResearch.finding: Winehog (2020) says Méo-Camuzet owns 0.1983 ha in the west end of La Vigne au Saint, the cadastral area of N 0085, which is recorded to the GFA Saint Vincent La Vigne au Saint. No filing links that GFA to Méo-Camuzet.
externalResearch.appNote: Winehog’s 0.1983 ha for Méo-Camuzet equals this parcel’s area; the recorded holder is an unlinked GFA. Area match only.

externalResearch.title: Bouchard: Le Corton plots 8 and 9
externalResearch.finding: Winehog (2020) says Bouchard’s red Le Corton includes cadastre plots 8 and 9. C 0008 and C 0009, recorded to Maison Bouchard Père et Fils in 2019–2024, were merged into C 0121 (DFI 2024) and divided into today’s C 0124 and C 0125 (DFI 2025), which have no company record yet. The DFI lineage is partial in scope.
externalResearch.appNote: Winehog (2020) names Le Corton plots 8 and 9 as Bouchard’s; DFI lineage carries them to this parcel with partial scope. Not farming.

externalResearch.title: Chandon de Briailles: Clos du Roi and Maréchaudes parcels
externalResearch.finding: The estate’s parcel areas (Clos du Roi 0.3505 and 0.096 ha; Maréchaudes 0.2742 and 0.123 ha) equal the cadastral areas of D 0005, D 0003, E 0098 and E 0105, all recorded to the domaine’s company. The pages are undated.
externalResearch.appNote: The estate’s stated parcel area equals this parcel’s cadastral area exactly; the parcel is recorded to its company. Not farming.

externalResearch.title: Vougeraie: Clos du Roi area
externalResearch.finding: Vougeraie states 0.497 ha for its Corton Clos du Roi (2024 page), the cadastral area of D 0011, recorded to Les Petits Fils de Pierre Ponnelle, which SFG La Vougeraie presides.

accessGaps: Tier 2 screened 349 free filings (about 8,400 PDF pages) of 105 companies by OCR and read the schedules and lease recitals it cites from page images or text layers. It is not an exhaustive reading of every corporate archive. Paid land-registry (SPF) copies and outreach remain Tier 3.
Fourteen operating-company filings without contribution or merger content were deliberately not OCR-screened.
Private individuals are absent from the legal-entity file: 341 parcels have no matched company record. Published holdings compare whole named-area totals and do not assign those parcels.

No filing reviewed is a signed current lease plus evidence of actual operation. Lease recitals in statutes (Latour GFAs to 2026 and 2031, Les Chagnots, Mémoire de Vignes, Vincent Rapet) and mandates (Esprit 20, L’Empereur) do not prove current farming.

Several recited leases have lapsed on their stated terms (Beaumonts 2008/2014, Gille 2013, Sordoillet 2020) and renewals are not recited; the Belgrand-, Marchal- and Rolland-Latour leases end on 10 November 2026.

Five provisional identifiers remain without a SIREN: SC Dom Hippolyte Thevenot, GFA Dom Emile Voarick, SCI des Bressandes, SCI Royland and the Beaune water syndicate; SCI des Domaines Dupray’s name matches a separately recorded SIREN in this cru.
The free filing index mislabels two Latour filings (each appears under the other company); their content was read and attributed by the company named in the document.

Winehog’s subscriber-only parcel details were not accessed; its free parts were read. Estate pages for Domaine Parent (HTTP 429), Château Corton C, Pavelot, Tollot-Beaut, Chevalier and Dublère were unavailable or gave no Corton area.
Bouchard’s 2026 partial asset contribution does not itemise which vineyards moved to the new Bouchard Père et Fils company; the 2025 rights file predates it.
Source boundaries, failed notice downloads and unsearched intervals are reported in the history coverage; none means no historical record.
Current farming remains unconfirmed for every parcel.
